name: Arc de Triomphe de l'Étoile

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/226413508 (centroid of the outline; the outline is square to heading 115.04° within 0.01 m — the Champs-Élysées façade faces east-south-east)

rights.note: Begun 1806 to Chalgrin's design, inaugurated 1836. Sculpture by François Rude (died 1855), Jean-Pierre Cortot (died 1843), Antoine Étex (died 1888), James Pradier (died 1852) and others of the 1830s. The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier dates from 1921 and the flame from 1923 (bronze by Edgar Brandt, died 1960, to Henri Favier's design): both are shown only as simple volumes (a slab, a small bronze rosette). Every author died more than 70 years ago.

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q64436_arc_de_triomphe.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. Overall, arch and pillar dimensions are the published ones; the cadastre outline in OpenStreetMap (47.3 × 24.4 m) is read as the projecting cornice. The heights of the entablature, frieze, attic, bas-reliefs and group pedestals are estimated from photographs (±5 %). All sculpture is stylised (groups of figures, winged geniuses, Fames, a procession on the frieze, framed battle reliefs), not a likeness of the works. The 30 attic shields are split 10 + 5 + 10 + 5 and the engraved names are drawn as lines. The model includes the paved island (terre-plein) of the Place Charles-de-Gaulle out to its kerb (r ≈ 57.4 m) with the chained bollards placed from OpenStreetMap and the two stairways down to the Passage du Souvenir; the roundabout road is not included. The island is flat in the model; the real ground falls 2–3 m across it, so the kerb skirt goes down 4 m. Paving patterns are simplified.
